newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sells more Telkom shares.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sells more Telkom shares.

text.p: The Indonesian government said on Wednesday it was making a block sale of 388 million shares of the state telecommunications giant Telkom to raise $600 million to accelerate payments on high-interest foreign debt.

This represented 4.15 percent of the paid up capital of PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) of 9.3 billion shares. Telkom floated 1.4 billion shares, or 15 percent of its capital, in November last year.
Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad told parliament the government had set a price for the block sale at between 3,400 and 3,650 rupiah ($1.45-$1.55).
"As a continuation of the privatisation of PT Telkom, the government has decided to sell further of its shares based on market conditions," Mar'ie said.

He said the proceeds would amount to a net of $600 million and would be used to accelerate repayment of high interest foreign debt by the government. In its initial flotation last year, Telkom placed its shares simultaneously with the Jakarta, Surabaya and New York stock exchanges.
Telkom's price fell 25 rupiah to close at 3,850 rupiah on a volume of 9.5 million shares in Jakarta on Wednesday after hitting a high of 4,075 rupiah in early afternoon trading.

"It is an anti-climax for the market. Previously rumours were saying the government might sell 15 percent of its existing stake, but then finally it is less than five percent," Asia Equity analyst Stephen Doe said.
He said since the government decided to sell in a block, it would not have much short-term impact on the price as the total number of shares available in the market would not immediately increase.
Indra Novan Ginting, analyst of PT Bank Negara Indonesia Securities, said the buyers would be fund managers who were usually long-term investors.
"I don't think it will have much impact on Telkom's price for the rest of this year," Indra said.
Indra also said the price offer was fair.

"If we look at the 30-year, long-term bond yield in the United States and compare it to Telkom earnings price per share, I think a fair value would be 3,700 rupiah. So this ranging price is fair enough," he said.

Mar'ie said the government had appointed state-owned PT Danareksa Sekuritas and PT Bahana Securities as its placement agents in Indonesia, while Deutsche Morgan Grenfell would act as its agent in the United States.
